candidate_title: Flexible model composition in machine learning and its implementation in MLJ
candidate_abstract: The paper sets out a graph-based composition protocol, termed learning networks, in which assorted machine-learning models form meta-models. It demonstrates that this approach overcomes several composition limitations found in leading machine-learning platforms. Simple examples introduce the protocol, followed by a compact notation for specifying networks within the MLJ framework. This notation can express Wolpert-style model stacking with out-of-sample predictions for the base learners.

candidate_title: MCP-Solver: Integrating Language Models with Constraint Programming Systems
candidate_abstract: MCP Solver connects large language models to symbolic solvers using the Model Context Protocol, an open-source standard for AI system integration. The combination addresses a key limitation of language models by adding formal solving and reasoning capabilities while retaining their strengths. The implementation exposes constraint programming through Minizinc, propositional satisfiability through PySAT, and satisfiability modulo theories through Python Z3. Model editing is coupled to repeated validation so that modifications remain consistent and can be refined in a structured way.
